title: Airtable AI assistant for record checks and intake work
h1: an airtable assistant that learns the table before writing
description: Review Airtable records, inspect fields and prepare intake work with Metal. Copy three routines and see why record edits need explicit limits.
answer: **find the missing owner before the launch stalls.** an airtable bot can inspect your base, list records and open a row before handing you the gaps. name the base and table, then start read only. when the reports are right, you can allow intake rows, attachment uploads or corrections under rules you choose.
og_line: read the fields before filling the rows.

app.name: Airtable
app.intro: **get the gaps that stop work, with the row beside each.** find the right base, read its field definitions and open the records that need attention. your team's column names can hide rules; tell the bot what each required field means before allowing writes.

highlight.use: find the base that holds this week's launch work
learn what owner, ready and due mean in your table
pull the content due this week
open the row with a missing owner before flagging it
read the comment that might already answer the venue question
look at the asset attached to the content row
add the intake rows you agreed to, in the right fields
correct the field you asked it to fix

app.setup:
**start the first review read only.**

connect airtable in **connected apps** and give your records bot read-only access. name the base and table. ask it to describe the fields it will use.

when you allow writing, choose the exact actions the job needs. an intake bot doesn't need field or table changes.

routines_intro: **start with the table that keeps catching you out.** name its fields and explain what counts as missing. these routines read fresh records or files each time.

routines.name: editorial readiness check
routines.message: every monday at 9, read my airtable content table. find records due this week with missing titles, owners or assets. list missing values here. inspect attachment details where needed. leave publishing status and dates alone.
routines.output: a short list of content gaps to fix before publishing

routines.name: event logistics gaps
routines.message: every thursday at noon, read upcoming records in my airtable event table. compare them with the venue and contact checklist in your memory notes. read record comments before calling a question unanswered. list gaps and uncertain answers here. never edit the records.
routines.output: venue and contact questions that still need an answer

routines.name: approved intake capture
routines.message: every weekday at 5, read new intake files in my project folder named approved intake. inspect the destination airtable fields. compare each item with existing records using the matching rule in your memory notes. show proposed new rows here and ask before adding them. report unclear matches instead of overwriting records. skip any item already present.
routines.output: new intake rows after your review, with uncertain matches held back

asks:
**get a useful review before handing over edits.** read only lets the bot find gaps and show proposed rows in chat. airtable changes skip sending approval; the intake routine asks because its instruction says to.

when you allow writing:

- choose record creation or correction only when needed
- leave field changes, table changes and deletion out
- write "ask me before you change anything" for supervised edits
cannot: **write with read-only access.** it cannot add rows, upload attachments or repair records. it can show proposed values in chat.
**guess what blank means.** tell it whether an empty field means missing, unnecessary or waiting for a decision.
**prove an item is new from its title.** give a matching rule. send unclear matches to you instead of overwriting.
**run on a sleeping computer.** local jobs need an awake machine and open dusk app. cloud keeps them available with your computer off.

sections.h: tell it what your fields mean
sections.md:
**ready can mean three different things in the same company.** tell the bot which fields it should read and fill, which values are required and how to find existing records.

a note column may carry a team rule nobody wrote into its name. explain it before allowing writes.

mostly cells and formulas? compare [google sheets](/integrations/google-sheets). work starts in a page? try [notion](/integrations/notion).

**small batches make bad matches easier to catch.** name one target table and keep approved intake in a folder the bot can read.

after creating rows, ask it to return the saved records. compare those values with the source files. use a [filing routine](/use-cases/file-organizer) to plan where supporting files belong.

faq.q: can chatgpt work with my airtable base?
faq.a: **yes, through a connected airtable account.** choose the bot's ai in dusk. name the base and ask for the missing owners in one table.

faq.q: can it add records without changing the table structure?
faq.a: **yes. allow only record creation and its lookups.** leave field and table changes out. the intake routine asks before adding rows because you told it to.

faq.q: what is a useful airtable routine for everyday work?
faq.a: **find the gap that will delay friday.** missing content owners, absent assets and unanswered event questions make useful first jobs. all can stay read only.

review.by: lead agent: independent reviewer pass against seo/facts (4 reviewers), every finding applied, automated gate

steps: connect airtable with read only access
ask for records due this week without an owner
open the flagged rows and compare them with the report

mistakes.mistake: treating every blank as an error
mistakes.fix: explain which fields must have a value and which can stay empty.

mistakes.mistake: adding rows without checking for existing records
mistakes.fix: give a matching rule and hold uncertain matches for your decision.

tip.text: a list of three missing owners beats a tidy summary that hides them.
